question: Can a guest crafting vsock packets with a forged src_cid make the HOST deliver a connection/datagram attributed to a CID other than the one the host assigned (3271)?
verdict: HOLDS (A-8/K-A1 confirmed; forged src_cid is dropped by the host, never delivered as a foreign CID)
forge_mechanism: kretprobe on virtio_transport_get_local_cid() in the guest kernel (vermagic 7.0.0-29-generic), overriding the return so the guest common layer stamps a forged src_cid into every outgoing virtio_vsock_hdr
note_results_jsonl: the raw results.jsonl on-host had a cosmetic grep -c '0\n0' artifact in zero-count fields; the integers below are the verified counts from listener.log/capture.log and match the streamed driver output

scenarios.note: STREAM+SEQPACKET both accepted; host attributes the real CID 3271; full handshake on the wire (REQUEST 3271->2, RESPONSE 2->3271)
forged REQUESTs (src_cid=3272) reached the host wire via the vhost tap but were dropped; no host RESPONSE; guest connect() ETIMEDOUT(110); host accepted nothing
forging the host's own CID (2) is likewise dropped (src_cid 2 != guest_cid 3271); ETIMEDOUT

connection established and attributed to real 3271; the PRE message delivered; after flipping forge on, the forged-src_cid packet was dropped and the connection stayed attributed to 3271 (no re-attribution)

subclaims.connection: HOLDS - forged-src_cid REQUEST dropped; no accept with foreign CID
subclaims.datagram_seqpacket: HOLDS - forged-src_cid SEQPACKET dropped; no recv with foreign CID
subclaims.across_handshake: HOLDS - established connection stays bound to the real CID; mid-stream forged packets dropped
